scope: All 31 verses read: text for sense and metre, translation and word glosses against the text. The print is corrupt in places (SOURCES §10.3); the text was not compared with the source page. Verse 31 remains obscure.

items.issue: The second half is a wish for the next birth — to be the hunter to the cuckoo, Rāhu to the moon, Śiva’s eye-fire to Love, and Love to her lord. It had been read as a list of enemies “against my beloved”.
items.change: Retranslated; the “obscure” note removed; words re-glossed.

items.issue: The verse addresses the beloved (kānte) but was translated in the third person (“her eye … her heart”).
kim ity adbhutam closes a paradox (one wagtail makes kings, two make wretches): “how strange!”, not “what wonder?”.
The verse answers verse 7 and turns on a pun: daityaguru, the demons’ teacher, is Śukra, and śukra is seed. It had been translated as “her lover’s teacher released her” and marked obscure.
items.change: Retranslated with the pun explained; words re-glossed.

items.issue: “her lover” in a verse spoken in the first person.
The verse is addressed to a water-jar (kumbhavara), which after beating, drying, kneading and firing rides on a woman’s hip. It was “jar-bearer”, and the swing was “of a lover’s arms”.
prasūtatanayā is “whose daughter has given birth” (hence the visit to the son-in-law), not “who had a baby”.

Marked obscure, but the sense is plain once dastinaḥ is read as hastinaḥ: the antelopes, beaten by the women’s eyes, had the wit to leave; the elephants, beaten by their breasts, stay on in their pride.

items.change: Removed; the compound rendered more fully.

items.issue: kim arājanyakam atra rājate is “does kinglessness prevail here?” (said to one who steals a heart and walks off), not “unroyal … as if royal”.
items.change: Now “Is there no king in this land?”.

items.issue: The speech belongs to the eyes (nau, “us two”), who have gone to the ears to disclaim blame; the translation had mixed the speakers.
madarpita is “given by me”: he asks for his embrace and kisses back. It was “the embrace you gave me”.
Typo caiḥ for cauraiḥ in the word gloss.
mukhacchāyā is the radiance of the face, not its “shade”.
Quarter 3 reads māṃ navayauvanāṃ śaśimukhīṃ…, two syllables short of the metre (17 for 19). The usual text is māṃ dṛṣṭvā navayauvanāṃ…, “seeing me”.
options: A. Restore dṛṣṭvā and log it.
B. Keep the print’s reading with the note in the translation.
items.recommend: A: the metre proves the loss and the sense needs the word.

items.issue: dastinaḥ in quarter 3 is not a word; hastinaḥ (“elephants”) is certainly meant.
Quarter 4 reads kaṃdarpa haranetradīdhitiriyaṃ; the usual text is kandarpe haranetradīdhitir ahaṃ (“may I be the fire of Śiva’s eye upon Love”). The translation follows the usual sense.
items.recommend: A: the parallel locatives (bandhane, paridhvaṃse, prāṇeśvare) require kandarpe.

items.issue: svedaṃ vṛthā vahasi (“you bear sweat in vain”) is probably khedaṃ (“grief”), the usual reading; the translation has “shed sweat”.
options: A. Emend to khedaṃ and translate “why do you grieve in vain”.

items.issue: Verse 31 is still obscure to me and is marked so on the page; quarter 2 of verse 28 (śocāmi yat tava kim atra virodham anyat) is also doubtful.
options: B. You supply the sense or a better text.
